name: edit_doc
description: Surgical find-and-replace on an existing wiki markdown document. Replaces `old_string` with `new_string` exactly once (or every occurrence with `replace_all`). The surrounding context must still be unique to avoid ambiguity. Returns the commit SHA, the unified diff, and any broken markdown links the edit introduces. Errors with "old_string not found" or "matched multiple times" — in those cases provide more surrounding context or set `replace_all`. USAGE GUIDANCE: prefer one `edit_doc` per logical change. When you have multiple related edits to the same doc, use `multi_edit` instead of firing several `edit_doc` calls.

path.description: Wiki-relative path to the markdown file. Must end in `.md` and the file must already exist.

old_string.description: The text to replace. Include enough surrounding context to make the match unique. Must be different from `new_string`.

new_string.description: The replacement text. Whitespace/indentation in this string is preserved verbatim — choose it to match the surrounding document.

replace_all.description: If true, replace every occurrence of `old_string`. Defaults to false (exactly-one match required).

commit_message.description: Short commit message summarizing the change.

base_sha.description: Optional. The sha you last read for `path` (returned by `read_doc`). When set, the edit aborts with `stale_base` if HEAD has moved since — re-read with `read_doc` and retry. Strongly recommended over MCP; the chat agent can omit it (the loop has direct state).

expires_in_seconds.description: Optional. How long (in seconds) you anticipate continuing to work on this file or feature before you're done. Sets the TTL on your row in the Active agents list, replacing the 24h default — use a smaller value for a focused short session, a larger one when you expect to be on the same task for hours. You only have ONE row in the list at a time per (user, agent), so the latest write's value wins. Range: 60 to 604800 (7 days).
